item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially preferable because it implements the requested API with the established multipart helper and avoids A’s explicit contract violations and unrelated API expansion. Neither patch fully satisfies the contract because both duplicate FilesService.Add instead of routing Upload through it.","reasons":["B preserves FilesOption behavior and uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile directly, as required.","A adds six association options and multipart field machinery despite the contract explicitly forbidding association fields and changes to FilesOption behavior.","A unnecessarily expands internal/multipartbody with Field and NewFileWithFields, while the contract requires reuse of the existing NewFile helper.","Both implementations directly call Raw.Do and duplicate Add’s request/response logic instead of delegating to FilesService.Add; this is the main defect in B as well as A."],"risks_a":["Introduces prohibited public APIs: WithFileDealID, WithFilePersonID, WithFileOrganizationID, WithFileProductID, WithFileActivityID, and WithFileLeadID.","Changes FilesOption semantics by adding multipart form state.","Duplicates Add’s request construction, decoding, and error handling rather than routing through Add, creating maintenance drift risk."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add’s request path instead of simply calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...).","Tests do not verify uploaded content, Upload retry behavior with streamed content, validation cases, or source-reader error propagation.","The exported Upload method lacks a Go documentation comment, and its combined validation error is less precise than separate filename/content errors."]}
